scenario: LEXP.7.20 with [LNUL.4.1]: a nullable schema-typed slot left unset is `null`, and a `null` operand of `==` or `!=` propagates, so the `where` is not satisfied either way. The host asserts Parent 1 and Child 1 with `parent` null, and pumps once. Neither `eq` (`c.parent == p`) nor `ne` (`c.parent != p`) fires; `unset` (`c.parent is null`) fires, so the Child was matched and the slot read was `null`. Exactly ["unset 1"]. A runtime that compared a null reference as an id (rete id 0, or a fact that is never live) would answer `!=` true and log `ne 1/1`. PATH PINNED: the join test's comparison, scanned, with one `null` operand; libds `rete/eval.c` BINOP comparison arm (Kleene null before `val_eq_unordered`), Mercury `ds.eval` `compare_outcome`.
rules_ds:
schema Parent scope logical:
    id: Int key

schema Child scope logical:
    id: Int key
    parent: Parent? mutable

rule eq:
    Child c
    Parent p where c.parent == p
->
    log info "eq {c.id}/{p.id}"

rule ne:
    Child c
    Parent p where c.parent != p
->
    log info "ne {c.id}/{p.id}"

rule unset:
    Child c where c.parent is null
->
    log info "unset {c.id}"
